ctor.rationale: `base(2, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (TheBomb.cs:23-26) == cost 2 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / SELF. No keywords.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DynamicVar("Turns", 3m)` + `new DynamicVar("BombDamage", 40m)` (TheBomb.cs:17-21) == both numbers, both declared. 40 is the largest single damage number in the pool.

OnPlay.rationale: `(await PowerCmd.Apply<TheBombPower>(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars["Turns"].BaseValue, Owner.Creature, this)).SetDamage(DynamicVars["BombDamage"].BaseValue)` (TheBomb.cs:30) == `PowerCmd.apply(..., TheBombPower, self._turns, ...)` then a re-fetch by id and `power.set_damage(self._damage)` (colorless_skills.py:741-743). The Turns value is the power's AMOUNT and the damage is set separately on both sides, which is the part that is easy to swap.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars["BombDamage"].UpgradeValueBy(10m)` (TheBomb.cs:35) == `self._damage += 10` (40 -> 50). The TURNS var stays 3 when upgraded on both sides -- the bomb does not land sooner, it lands harder.

guards.what: C# dereferences the Apply result WITHOUT a null check; the sim re-fetches by id and skips on None (TheBomb.cs:30 vs colorless_skills.py:741-743)
guards.issue: This is the INVERSE of card/crimson_mantle's and card/inferno's `?.` finding: those two use the null-conditional operator and so skip their follow-up call when Apply returns null, while The Bomb uses a bare `.` and would throw a NullReferenceException. `PowerCmd.Apply<T>` documents three null cases (PowerCmd.cs:29-34): combat ending, `!target.CanReceivePowers`, and a stacking `ModifyAmount` that resolves to 0. So in the game, playing a second The Bomb whose amount was modified to 0 CRASHES, and in the sim it silently applies no extra damage. DORMANT, and deliberately not labelled live: reproducing a crash is not a fidelity target, no ported effect modifies a positive self-applied buff down to exactly 0 (Artifact intercepts only debuffs, cmds.py:299-306), and the other two null cases imply the combat is already over. Recorded because the sim's re-fetch pattern is SAFER than the source here, which is worth stating explicitly rather than leaving as an apparent match.
